name: Native Vertebral Osteomyelitis / Discitis
definition: Infection involving vertebral bodies and/or adjacent disc space, commonly hematogenous in adults; delayed recognition can cause neurological injury, deformity or sepsis.

typical: Persistent focal back or neck pain
Risk increases with bloodstream infection, endocarditis or susceptible host states

investigations.principle: In suspected native vertebral osteomyelitis, obtain microbiological and inflammatory-marker evidence and define spinal involvement.
investigations.labs: IDSA recommends two sets of blood cultures plus baseline ESR and CRP.
investigations.MRI: IDSA recommends spine MRI in suspected native vertebral osteomyelitis.
investigations.microbiology: When stable and without neurological compromise/sepsis, establish microbiological diagnosis before empiric antibiotics when feasible.

green: Monitor clinical response and inflammatory markers
amber: Hemodynamic instability, sepsis or severe/progressive neurological symptoms require urgent empiric treatment alongside attempts to establish microbiological diagnosis.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Do not label pyogenic or tuberculous spinal infection as an Ayurvedic disease equivalent. Any Ayurveda supportive discussion must remain separate from antimicrobial/surgical standards of care.

patientEducation.summary: Infection involving vertebral bodies and/or adjacent disc space, commonly hematogenous in adults; delayed recognition can cause neurological injury, deformity or sepsis.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for new/progressive major weakness, gait deterioration, bladder/bowel dysfunction, saddle sensory loss, fever/systemic illness with severe spinal pain, or cancer-associated neurological symptoms.

sources.title: Clinical Practice Guidelines for Native Vertebral Osteomyelitis in Adults
sources.note: Published 2015; still used here as an authoritative specialty guideline; evidence date is explicitly retained.
